clue.text: Difficult to get cottage, for example? Bad luck!

parts.note: difficult means hard
cottage cheese is one kind of cheese, so cottage exemplifies it

explanation.surface: Someone complains that cottages are hard to come by, and a friend commiserates.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD CHEESE is a British idiom of mock sympathy, roughly 'tough luck'; the question mark flags that cottage is an example of a cheese, not a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom of sympathy, often ironic, for a misfortune someone has suffered.

clue.text: It's second nature to dress

definitions.meaning: something done by long custom without thinking
a distinctive costume, as a nun's or a rider's

explanation.surface: Something becomes second nature, like the act of getting dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom so ingrained it is automatic; also the garment of a monk or rider.

clue.text: Going to play, regard one small instrument

indicators.note: letters going off to play are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone about to perform regards a single small instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to play' rearranges REGARD and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact keyboard instrument whose sound comes from vibrating metal reeds, like a harmonium.

clue.text: Changing the case for a rights issue, for example

definitions.meaning: switching letters from lower to upper case
a rights issue raises a company's share capital

explanation.surface: A company alters its legal case to justify issuing new shares.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is turning lower-case letters into capitals; the other is the share capital of a company, which a rights issue raises.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing letters as capitals; also the total share capital a company raises, for instance through issuing new shares.

clue.text: It identifies the outcome of a bear market

indicators.note: what comes out of the words that follow is a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A financial commentator notes what a falling stock market leaves behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outcome of' signals letters that come out of bEAR MARKet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag or nick in a sheep's ear identifies its owner.

clue.text: Pickwickian doctor in prison

definitions.meaning: Dr ..., a character in The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A doctor from a Dickens novel ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Slammer is a hot-tempered army surgeon in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dickens character's surname, and an informal slang word for a jail.

clue.text: Stick used to drive young animal round pound

indicators.note: the young animal goes round the pound sign, enclosing it

parts.note: a cub is the young of a bear, fox or lion
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A farmer uses a stick to drive a young animal around an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like an animal enclosure; it is the money sign L.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer drives the ball with a wooden or metal stick of this kind.

clue.text: Flower left out of bed in the end

indicators.note: puts the word in at the end of the answer

parts.note: someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets up and leaves a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of bed' looks like gardening but just means UP; 'the end' places IN last.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Beloved subject of musical

explanation.surface: A lover is the theme of a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boy Friend is a 1950s Sandy Wilson musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sweetheart; also the title of Sandy Wilson's stage show.

clue.text: Financial guarantee exploded in morose story — paper's lead

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter
blown apart, so the letters of the words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy newspaper story is the lead item about a blown-up financial pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploded' rearranges INMOROSESTORY; 'paper's lead' supplies P, which goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A written signed promise to pay a stated sum, so a financial undertaking.

clue.text: Clipped item relating to doctor's calling

definitions.text: Clipped item relating to doctor's calling

parts.words: Clipped item relating to doctor's calling
parts.note: a device clipped to the belt that beeps when a doctor is being called, not anything about the profession

explanation.surface: A trimmed object connected with the medical vocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' suggests a vocation, but it means a summons; 'Clipped' means attached by a clip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager clipped to clothing that beeps to summon a hospital doctor.

clue.text: Decline a prize

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb meaning refuse; it is a noun, a wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasting away of tissue or a gradual deterioration, as with unused muscles.

clue.text: Its owner is sure to feed the fishes

definitions.text: Its owner is sure to feed the fishes

parts.words: Its owner is sure to feed the fishes
parts.note: 'feed the fishes' usually means drowning or seasickness, but here an owner literally feeds stocks of fish being bred

explanation.surface: Someone is doomed to drown or be seasick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feed the fishes' is slang for drowning or being sick over the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm raising a particular freshwater game fish, whose keeper feeds the stock.

clue.text: Man of 49 said to be ineligible to vote

indicators.note: spoken words, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a minor, under age, cannot vote

explanation.surface: A man aged 49 claims to be barred from voting.
explanation.walkthrough: '49' is not an age: forty-niners were the prospectors of the 1849 California gold rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector digging for gold in the 1849 California rush was a forty-niner.

clue.text: Provide endless entertainment befitting a king

indicators.note: endless here means literally without an end, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: regale, as a noun, is a lavish feast or entertainment

explanation.surface: Laying on non-stop entertainment fit for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' looks like it means non-stop; it drops the last E of REGALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal or kingly in manner, as suits a monarch.

clue.text: In practice, judges gripped by bona-fide case

indicators.note: the bona-fide word forms the outer case

parts.note: bona fide means genuine, real
a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: In legal practice, judges are taken up with a genuine case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal but marks the bona-fide word as the outer shell; 'gripped by' puts the judges' word inside it. The definition is 'practice', with 'In' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice run of a play or concert before the real performance.

clue.text: One edging along a footpath

parts.note: not someone shuffling along a path, but a block forming the edge of the pavement

explanation.surface: A person inching along a pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edging' suggests moving slowly; it means forming an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone block forming the edge of a pavement beside the road.

clue.text: Madam Butterfly, for example, can at the end drag on

parts.note: Madam Butterfly is a Puccini opera
a can is a tin

indicators.note: the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A performance of Puccini's opera can drag on towards its finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag on' reads as a phrase but 'on' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is on is running or functioning.

clue.text: Crews with fish getting a greeting

parts.note: a ship's crew are its hands
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Sailors with their catch receive a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another's palm is a common form of hello.

clue.text: Extra subjects in the classical sixth?

definitions.text: Extra subjects in the classical sixth?

parts.words: Extra subjects in the classical sixth?
parts.note: sounds like extra classes studied by a sixth-former doing Classics; really Latin for things to be added

explanation.surface: Additional subjects studied by sixth-formers taking Classics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sixth' suggests the sixth form, the last two years of British school; 'classical' points to Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural for items to be added, as supplementary material in a book.

clue.text: In English wood, church camp

indicators.note: the church goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: pine is a wood
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church encampment in an English forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' looks like a tent site; it means effeminate.
explanation.definitionFit: Effeminate or androgynous in manner, like the adjective for theatrical flamboyance.

clue.text: Adore strange mountainous girl

indicators.note: the letters are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone adores an odd girl from the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges ADORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain nymph in Greek mythology, so a maiden of the mountains.

clue.text: Mrs Asquith's clipped language

indicators.note: cut short, losing its first letter

parts.note: Margot Asquith was the wife of Prime Minister H. H. Asquith

explanation.surface: The wife of a British prime minister spoke tersely.
explanation.walkthrough: Margot Asquith was the wife of H. H. Asquith, British prime minister 1908-16; 'clipped' takes off her M.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon or slang particular to a group, so a kind of language.

clue.text: Devour chine

definitions.meaning: a deep narrow ravine, especially on the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: Eat up a cut of pork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chine' looks like a cut of meat; it is also a deep ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat greedily; also a narrow ravine, which a chine also is.

clue.text: One used to parlour work gives help to large numbers that are retired

indicators.note: withdrawn, drawn back, so read backwards

parts.note: a myriad is a huge number
aid means help

explanation.surface: A worker helps a crowd of retired people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that are retired' turns the large-numbers word round; 'parlour' is a milking parlour, not a sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who milks cows, working in the milking shed.

clue.text: Sort of courage a wife may show

definitions.meaning: the courage that comes from drinking

explanation.surface: The bravery a wife might display.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch courage is bravery from drink; 'my old Dutch' is Cockney for a wife (from duchess).
explanation.definitionFit: Courage from alcohol; also London slang for a spouse.

clue.text: Carving iron is left in joint

indicators.note: one piece put inside the other
carving cuts up and reshapes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carving iron is left in the roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carving' rearranges IRON IS to SIRION, with L put in.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime cut of beef from the loin, roasted as a joint.

clue.text: Single-minded tripper

parts.note: single-minded as in minding only oneself; tripper as one on an ego trip

explanation.surface: A determined holidaymaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single-minded' suggests determination; it means thinking only of number one.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person, always on an ego trip.

clue.text: Spill the beans, say, and find another vegetable

indicators.note: spoken words, so heard, not spelt

parts.note: to leak is to spill the beans

explanation.surface: Spill the beans and you'll find a different vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beans' sets up a vegetable patch; 'Spill the beans' means reveal a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion-family plant with a long white stem, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: If you're on someone else's, you're both in tune

definitions.text: If you're on someone else's, you're both in tune

parts.words: If you're on someone else's, you're both in tune
parts.note: being on the same radio frequency as another person means sharing their thinking

explanation.surface: Two people sharing a frequency are in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio frequency, figuratively the shared way of thinking of two people.
